nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ﴾.
The meaning may be: the sending down of the Book is from Allah [Translator's note: i.e. "from Allah" is its khabar (predicate)].
Or the meaning may be: this is the sending down of the Book.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَٱعْبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصاً لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ﴾.
That is: in accordance with what was made true in the [earlier] scriptures about its being sent down to you.
And the meaning may be: He made it binding upon you, by His right over you and over His creation.
And it is said that the meaning is: it commands justice and truth.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَٱعْبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصاً لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ﴾.
That is: do not worship anything else along with Him.
And al-Farrāʾ related ﴿لَهُ الدِّينُ﴾ with al-dīn in the nominative.
And it is wrong from three angles:
The first: that after it comes ﴿ألاَ لِلَّهِ الدينُ الخَالِصُ﴾, which makes this unnecessary.
Also: it has not been read so.
Also: it makes ﴿مُخْلِصاً﴾ the full stop (al-tamām), whereas the full stop at the end of the verse is more fitting.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلاَ لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْخَالِصُ﴾.
That is: He alone is to be worshipped, because among people there are those who have a religion but do not make it purely for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿أَلاَ لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْخَالِصُ﴾: he said: "There is no god but Allah."
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلاَّ لِيُقَرِّبُونَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ زُلْفَىۤ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, a rank.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, only so that they intercede for us.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid: ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ قَالُوا مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ إلاَّ لِيُقَرّبُونَا إلى اللهِ زُلْفَى﴾.
And in the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy: ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أوْليَاءَ مَا نَعْبُدُكُمْ إلاَّ ليقرِّبُونَا إلَى اللهِ زُلْفَى﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and the reported speech (ḥikāya) in this is clear [Translator's note: i.e. an implied "saying" introduces their words].

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّوْ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَداً لاَّصْطَفَىٰ مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾.
The connection of this with the preceding indicates that these are among those who took protectors besides Allah.
And ﴿لاَّصْطَفَىٰ﴾: He would have chosen.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُكَوِّرُ ٱللَّيْـلَ عَلَى ٱلنَّهَـارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ ٱلنَّـهَارَ عَلَى ٱللَّيْلِ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, He casts this over that, and that over this.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the root meaning of al-takwīr in the language is wrapping and gathering together; from it is kawr al-ʿimāma (the winding of the turban), and from it is ﴿إذا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾.
﴿ثُمَّ﴾ here indicates that the second statement comes after the first.
And Qatāda said: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾ is Ḥawwāʾ; He created her from one of his ribs.
And it is said: His creating the mate is referred back to "one", i.e. to a soul on its own [Translator's note: i.e. "who created you from a single soul, alone, then made from it its mate"], then He made from it its mate.
That is, kinds [Translator's note: this gloss evidently belongs to the omitted continuation of the verse, ﴿وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾].
Mujāhid said: of camels two, of cattle two, of sheep two and of goats two.
Qatāda said: it is like the one in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَخْلُقُكُمْ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُـمْ خَلْقاً مِّن بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ﴾.
Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: a drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, until the creation is complete.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ ثَلاَثٍ﴾.
Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: in the darkness of the womb, in the darkness of the placenta, and in the darkness of the belly.
And it is said: in the loins, then in the womb, then in the belly; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda, and the first is sounder.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن تَكْفُرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنكُمْ، وَلاَ يَرْضَىٰ لِعِبَادِهِ ٱلْكُفْرَ، وَإِن يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ﴾.
That is: He is pleased with gratitude for you; and ﴿تَشْكُرُواْ﴾ indicated the [noun] gratitude [to which the pronoun refers] [Translator's note: the verse is quoted in the text as «وَإِن يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ»; the Qurʾānic wording is ﴿وَإِن تَشْكُرُواْ يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ﴾].

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَا رَبَّهُ مُنِيباً إِلَيْهِ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: sincere.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says anāba when he returned and repented.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلَهُ نِعْمَةً مِّنْهُ نَسِيَ مَا كَانَ يَدْعُوۤ إِلَيْهِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
That is: He gave it to him and made it freely his; and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ used to recite:
هُنَالِكَ إنْ يُسْتَخْوَلُوا المَالَ - يُخْوِلُوا * وإن يُسْأَلُوا يُعْطُوا، وإن يَيْسِرُوا يُغْلُوا
(There, if they are asked to bestow wealth, they bestow; if asked, they give; and if they cast lots at the gaming, they pay high.)
Then He said: ﴿نَسِيَ مَا كَانَ يَدْعُوۤ إِلَيْهِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
That is: he forgot that for which he used to call on Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, before.
And the meaning may be: he forgot Allah whom he used to call on, as He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ﴾.
And in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿قُلْ تَمَتَّعْ بِكُفْرِكَ قَلِيلاً﴾ there is the meaning of threat.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لِلَّهِ أَندَاداً لِّيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ﴾.
Al-Suddī said: the rivals are men whom he obeys in acts of disobedience.
And it is said: he worshipped idols.
And this is nearer to what is correct, because that is in the context of Allah's, Mighty and Majestic is He, reproaching them for worshipping them.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَآءَ ٱللَّيْلِ سَاجِداً وَقَآئِماً﴾.
That is: praying; and al-qunūt is obedience.
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: ﴿آنَآءَ ٱللَّيْلِ﴾ means its hours: its beginning, its middle and its end.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Akhfash said: the reading of whoever read ﴿أَمَّنْ هُوَ﴾? without doubling [i.e. «أَمَنْ»] is weak in Arabic, because the alif of interrogation does not lean on what precedes it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what al-Akhfash said is good; indicating it is that the one in Sūrat al-Naml was only read with doubling. And the meaning of his statement is that the speech leans on what precedes it; it has no khabar (predicate), but what precedes it indicates it, because He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لِلَّهِ أَنْدَاداً لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ﴾.
So He omitted the khabar, because the meaning is: Is one who is obedient like this one?
Or: Is one who is obedient better, or this one?
And this is the place of the ﴿أَمْ﴾ that means "bal", as the poet said:
أَفَتِلْكَ أَمْ وَحْشِيَّةٌ مَسْبُوْعَةٌ * خَذَلَتْ وَهَادِيَةُ الصِّوَارِ قِوَامُهَا
(Is it that one, or a wild cow whose calf the beasts of prey have taken, who lagged behind, while the herd's leader is her mainstay?)
And his saying:
أذلك أم جَأْبٌ يُطَارِدُ آتُناً * حَمَلْنَ فَأَدْنَى حَمْلِهِنَّ دُرُوْصُ
(Is it that, or a thick-set wild ass chasing she-asses that have conceived, the nearest of whose pregnancies is about to give birth?)
And for whoever reads without doubling, the khabar is also omitted; and this is something subtle in Arabic, with which only one practised in it is at ease, as the poet said:
فَأُقْسِمُ لَوْشَيْءٌ أتانَا رَسُوْلُهُ * سِوَاكَ، وَلَكِنْ لَمْ نَجِدْ لَكَ مَدْفَعاً
(I swear, had anything other than you sent its messenger to us — but we found no way to repel you.)
That is: "we would have repelled it"; the omission occurs in this way.
And it is said: it is a vocative (nidāʾ), i.e. "O you who stand [in prayer] in the hours of the night."
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَحْذَرُ ٱلآخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُواْ رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read ﴿يَحْذَرُ عَذَابَ الآخِرَةِ﴾, and the meaning is the same.
That is [Translator's note: this explains the following phrase of the verse, ﴿قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾]: just as the knowing and the ignorant are not equal, so the obedient and the disobedient are not equal.
And it is said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ what is theirs in obedience and what is against them in disobedience.
Then He said ﴿إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ ٱلأَلْبَابِ﴾, i.e. [those of] intellects.
And the lubb of everything is its pure essence.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ فِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌ وَأَرْضُ ٱللَّهِ وَاسِعَةٌ﴾.
It is said: the good is the Garden.
And it is said the meaning is: they have good in this world, i.e. good praise, and tranquillity in what they have.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَرْضُ ٱللَّهِ وَاسِعَةٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, so emigrate, and keep away from the idols.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱعْبُدُواْ مَا شِئْتُمْ مِّن دُونِهِ﴾.
[It is] by way of threat, and this was before the command to fight.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْخَاسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوۤاْ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
That is: they lost themselves by being consigned forever to the Fire, and their families by not entering the Garden, where they would have had families.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: there is no one but Allah has prepared for him a family in the Garden, if he obeys Him.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ يُخَوِّفُ ٱللَّهُ بِهِ عِبَادَهُ يٰعِبَادِ فَٱتَّقُونِ﴾.
That is: that punishment which has been described.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱجْتَنَبُواْ ٱلطَّاغُوتَ أَن يَعْبُدُوهَا﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: al-ṭāghūt is the devils.
Abū Jaʿfar said: we have explained this in Sūrat al-Baqara.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَبَشِّرْ عِبَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَمِعُونَ ٱلْقَوْلَ فَيَـتَّبِعُونَ أَحْسَنَهُ﴾.
There are two views on the meaning of this:
The first view: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ ٱلْقَوْلَ﴾ is the Qurʾān, and ﴿أَحْسَنَهُ﴾ is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded the prophets of obedience to Him, so they follow it.
And the other view: that they listen to the Qurʾān and to other things, and follow the Qurʾān.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is good, and the meaning is: when they hear of punishment and pardon, they pardon, and consider pardon to be better, even if the punishment is their right.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَنْ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ ٱلْعَذَابِ أَفَأَنتَ تُنقِذُ مَن فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾? [verse 19].
It is asked: how can two interrogatives be brought, when the grammarians are agreed that two interrogatives are not permissible in a noun and its khabar (predicate)?
There are two answers to this:
One of them: that when the speech grows long, the Arabs repeat [it] for emphasis (tawkīd); and Sībawayh said the same about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ، وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَابَاً وَعِظَاماً، أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ﴾?
The meaning on this [view] is: Is the one against whom the word of punishment has become due — will you then rescue him?
And the speech is a condition and its apodosis (jawāb), and the interrogative was brought to indicate making [the addressee] stop and acknowledge (al-tawqīf wa-l-taqrīr).
Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is: Will you rescue one against whom the word of punishment has become due?
Abū Jaʿfar said: this and the first are one.
And the other answer: that there is an omission in the speech.
And the meaning is: Will the one against whom the word of punishment has become due get free, or be saved?
Then He omitted the answer, and what comes after it is resumptive.
And the meaning is: Will the one of whom it is preceded in the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, that he will enter the Fire be saved or get free?

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَسَلَكَهُ يَنَابِيعَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It is narrated that all water in the earth has its origin in the sky.
And it may be that His sending it down is His creating it and bringing it into being by His command.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَسَلَكَهُ﴾ means He made it enter and made it ﴿يَنَابِيعَ﴾, the plural of yanbūʿ, on the pattern "yafʿūl" from nabaʿa, yanbaʿu (to spring forth).
﴿ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعاً مُّخْتَلِفاً أَلْوَانُهُ﴾, i.e. green, black, yellow and white.
﴿ثُمَّ يَهِـيجُ فَـتَرَاهُ مُصْفَـرّاً﴾, i.e. it dries up.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: it is said of a plant when its drying is complete: qad hāja, yahīju, hayjan.
﴿ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ حُطَاماً﴾, i.e. crumbled debris.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لأُوْلِي ٱلأَلْبَابِ﴾.
That is: they reflect, and so they remember that this points to the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and His power.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَن شَرَحَ ٱللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلإِسْلاَمِ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ﴾.
There is an omission in the speech.
And the meaning is: Is one whose breast Allah has opened, so that he is guided, like one upon whose heart He has set a seal, so that he is not guided?!
And in the ḥadīth, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Does the heart then expand? He said: Yes; when Allah brings light into it, it expands and becomes spacious. They said: Is there a sign of that? He said: Yes:
* withdrawing from the abode of delusion,
* turning to the abode of eternity,
* and preparing for death before [meeting] death."
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مِّن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ، أُوْلَـٰئِكَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
It is said: the meaning of ﴿مِن﴾ and "ʿan" here is the same.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is nothing; the meaning of ﴿مِّن﴾ is: when His verses are recited to them they grow hard [i.e. because of them], as He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَتْهُمْ رِجْساً إِلى رِجْسِهِمْ﴾.
And if one says "ʿan", its meaning is: their hearts grew hard and turned away from accepting the remembrance of Allah.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ كِتَاباً مُّتَشَابِهاً﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī narrated from ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: they said: O Messenger of Allah, tell us something. So there was revealed ﴿ٱللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿مُّتَشَابِهاً﴾ means it is not inconsistent.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and the meaning is that its parts resemble one another in wisdom and truth, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ لَوَجَدُواْ فِيهِ اخْتِلاَفاً كَثِيراً﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَّثَانِيَ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿مَثَانِي﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, repeated it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and the meaning is: that in which the stories, the reward and the punishment are repeated.
And it is said: al-mathānī is every sūra containing fewer than a hundred verses, i.e. they are repeated in prayer.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ، ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: they shiver at the verses in which punishment is mentioned, then they soften at the verses in which mercy is mentioned.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَن يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ سُوۤءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
There is an omission in the speech.
And the meaning is: Is one who shields himself with his face from the evil of the punishment like one who enters the Garden?
Mujāhid said: he falls on his face into the punishment on the Day of Resurrection.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and it is narrated that he is thrown into the Fire shackled, so he cannot shield himself from the Fire except with his face.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ، لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, without ambiguity.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is that it is straight, its parts not contradicting one another, because a crooked thing is inconsistent.
And it has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ﴾: not created.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً رَّجُلاً فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ﴾.
Qatāda said: he is the disbeliever, and the partners are the devils.
He said: ﴿وَرَجُلاً سَلَماً﴾ is the believer, who works for Allah alone.
Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: this is a parable for truth and falsehood, and the partners are the idols.
Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿مُتَشَاكِسُونَ﴾: at odds with one another.
Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever read ﴿رَجُلاً سَالِماً﴾ took it according to the verb [i.e. as an active participle], and whoever read ﴿سَلَماً﴾ made it a maṣdar (verbal noun), so its meaning is: one of complete belonging (dhā salam).

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ تَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾.
That is: the wronged will dispute with the wrongdoer, and the believer with the disbeliever.
Ibn ʿUmar said: we did not know what we would dispute about, until the civil strife (al-fitna) occurred, and we said: this is it.
And in the ḥadīth: al-Zubayr said: O Messenger of Allah, "shall we dispute on the Day of Resurrection after what was between us? He said: Yes, until to everyone who has a right his right is rendered. He said: then the matter is indeed severe."

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾.
Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدْقِ﴾, he says: he came with "There is no god but Allah"; ﴿وَصَدَّق بِهِ﴾ means [he believed] in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾, he says: they guarded themselves against associating partners [with Allah].
And Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from Manṣūr, who said: I said to Mujāhid: O Abū al-Ḥajjāj, what is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ﴾? [verse 33].
He said: the one who came with the Qurʾān and believed in it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this resembles the first view, and it is the view of most linguists.
And what indicates its correctness is that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read ﴿والَّذينَ جاءوا بالصِّدقِ وصَدَّقُوا به، أولئك هم المتَّقُونَ﴾.
So ﴿الَّذِي﴾ here and ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ are one.
And al-Ḥasan said: he is the believer, who comes with the truth on the Day of Resurrection, and believed in it in this world.
And some linguists say: the nūn was dropped from ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ because of the length of the noun [with its ṣila (relative clause)].
And some of them say: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ is in the sense of "alladhīna" (those who).
And some of them say: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ is a singular that conveys the meaning of a group.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and this view is the soundest of them: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ is like "man" (whoever), because no particular individual is intended by it; and its true sense is that the meaning is: "and the party that came with the truth and believed in it."
And other than this has been said about the verse.
Qatāda and Abū al-ʿĀliya said: the one who came with the truth is the Prophet ﷺ, and Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, [is the one who believed in it].
And it is said: the Prophet ﷺ and ʿAlī, peace be upon him.
ʿAlī ibn Saʿīd narrated to us: al-Ḥusayn ibn Naṣr narrated to us: my father narrated to me: ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدْقِ﴾ is Muḥammad ﷺ, ﴿وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ﴾ is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him.
And a parallel to "alladhī jāʾa bi-l-ṣidq", in its being a singular conveying [the meaning of] a group, is the poet's saying:
وإنَّ الَّذِي حَانَتْ بِفَلْجٍ دِمَاؤُهُمْ * هُمُ القَوْمُ كُلُّ القَوْمِ يَا أُمَّ خَالِد
(Those whose blood was spilt at Falj are the people, the people indeed, O Umm Khālid.)
And he dropped the nūn [Translator's note: i.e. in the dual relative «اللذا» for «اللذان»] in his saying:
أَبَنِي كُلَيْبٍ إنَّ عَمَيَّ اللَّذَا * قَتَلا المُلُوكَ وفَكَّكا الأَغْلاَلاَ
(O sons of Kulayb, my two uncles are the ones who killed kings and broke the fetters.)

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ وَيُخَوِّفُونَكَ بِٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِ﴾.
This indicates [promised] help; and most of the Kufans read ﴿بكافٍ عِبَادَهُ﴾.
And the singular is better, because it is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ is meant by it, and indicating this is ﴿وَيُخَوِّفُونَكَ بِٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: [those besides Him are] the idols.
Qatāda said: Khālid ibn al-Walīd took an axe to it [Translator's note: the text reads «أخذها خالد… فأساً»] and came to "al-ʿUzzā" to break it, and its custodian said to him: its force cannot be withstood, so beware of it. But he went on until he broke its nose.
And it is narrated that they said to the Prophet ﷺ: if you do not stop reviling them, we will command them to drive you mad.
Mujāhid said: this verse was revealed when the Prophet ﷺ recited Sūrat al-Najm at the door of the Kaʿba.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ يٰقَوْمِ ٱعْمَلُواْ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُـمْ إِنِّي عَامِلٌ فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُـمْ﴾ means according to your way.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a correct view.
And the meaning is: according to your way which you have chosen and which has become firmly established with you.
﴿إِنِّي عَامِلٌ﴾: the meaning is: I am working according to my way; then [this] was omitted.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلأَنفُسَ حِينَ مِوْتِـهَا وَٱلَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِـهَا﴾.
Jaʿfar ibn Abī al-Mughīra narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: the souls of the living and the souls of the dead are gathered, and they become acquainted with one another as long as Allah wills; then He withholds the one for which He has decreed death, and sends the other back to its body.
Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is ﴿وَٱلَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِـهَا﴾ [He takes] at the end of its term; and he said: "tawaffāhā" may mean He put it to sleep.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and it is said that the meaning is: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death by removing their breath and their discernment; then a verb was implied for the second, because it differs from the first.
So the meaning is: and He takes the one that has not died, in its sleep, by removing its discernment only, because the sleeper breathes.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the best that has been said on this is that ﴿يَتَوَفَّى﴾ and "yastawfī" have one meaning, [said] when a thing is taken in full, just as one says tabayyantu and istabantu, and tayaqqana and istayqana; so the dead person and the sleeper are one in this respect; and what indicates it is His saying ﴿فَيُمْسِكُ ٱلَّتِي قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ، وَيُرْسِلُ ٱلأُخْرَىٰ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ شُفَعَآءَ قُلْ أَوَلَوْ كَـانُواْ لاَ يَمْلِكُونَ شَيْئاً وَلاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: they said: we worshipped them only so that they would intercede for us.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَوْ كَـانُواْ لاَ يَمْلِكُونَ شَيْئاً وَلاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
Sībawayh said: this is the chapter of the wāw when the alif of interrogation enters upon it; that is your saying: "Is So-and-so with So-and-so?", and he says: "Is he one who would be with So-and-so?"
Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] said: this is by way of seeking guidance, or by way of disapproval; and what occurs of it in the Qurʾān means disapproval, affirmation (taqrīr), and the [actual] occurrence of the thing.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُل لِلَّهِ ٱلشَّفَاعَةُ جَمِيعاً﴾.
As He the Exalted said: ﴿مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ ٱشْمَأَزَّتْ قُلُوبُ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿ٱشْمَأَزَّتْ﴾: they were arrogant and disbelieved.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: they shrank.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says ishmaʾazza min kadhā when he recoiled from it.
And it is narrated that when they heard someone say "There is no god but Allah alone", they recoiled and said: our gods have not been mentioned.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَبَدَا لَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يَكُونُواْ يَحْتَسِبُونَ﴾.
It is narrated that they did deeds which they imagined would benefit them, but they did not benefit them, because they were associators.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَانَا، ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلْنَاهُ نِعْمَةً مِّنَّا﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿خَوَّلْنَاهُ﴾: We gave him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says khawwaltuhu kadhā, i.e. I gave it to him as a favour, not as a recompense.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ بَلْ هِيَ فِتْنَةٌ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ﴾ means on account of honour.
And Qatāda said: that is, on account of good that is in me.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: I have knowledge of earning, whether by trade or otherwise, so I knew that I would be given this.
And among the best that has been said on it: that the meaning is: I knew, when I was given this in this world, that I have a rank with Allah; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, rejected this from him and said: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أنَّ اللهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ مِهَ القُرُونِ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the wording is that of Q 28:78, ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ مِن قَبْلِهِ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ﴾, with «مِهَ» presumably a misprint for «مِنَ»] — the verse.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He does not give wealth to everyone who has a rank.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ هِيَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾.
That is: rather, the gift is a trial by which the servant is tested, so that it becomes manifest from him whether he is grateful or ungrateful.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ يٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُواْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ لاَ تَقْنَطُواْ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: it was revealed concerning "Waḥshī", the killer of Ḥamza — peace be upon Ḥamza — up to the completion of three verses. The Prophet ﷺ could not bear to look at him, so he thought that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, had not accepted his Islam from him; so these three verses were revealed.
And Ibrāhīm al-Taymī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he used to read: ﴿قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لاَ تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللهِ، إِنَّ اللهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبِ جَمِيعاً لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾.
And he said: it was revealed concerning the killer of Ḥamza and his kind; so he said.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and likewise it is narrated that it is [so] in the codex of Ibn Masʿūd.
And the meaning of ﴿لا تَقْنَطُواْ﴾ is: do not despair.
Qatāda said: ﴿وأنِيبُوا إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ﴾ means turn [to Him] and work for Him.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتَّبِعُـوۤاْ أَحْسَنَ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُـمْ مِّن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَكُـمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ بَغْتَةً﴾.
And all of it is good, so there are several views on this:
a- Among them: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has permitted retaliation — after wrong has been done — and pardon, and pardon is better.
b- Among them: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has informed about a people that they obeyed and about a people that they disobeyed, and commanded that we follow obedience.
c- Among them: that it is the abrogating [text].
d- Among them: that the meaning is: the good among what was sent down to you.
And ﴿بَغْتَةً﴾ means suddenly.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَن تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يٰحَسْرَتَا عَلَىٰ مَا فَرَّطَتُ فِي جَنبِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
The meaning is: do this for fear that a soul should say, and in dislike that a soul should say, "Alas, my regret!"
And al-ḥasra is remorse, i.e. there befalls a person that with which he becomes ḥasīr, i.e. worn out [Translator's note: the text has «معيباً»; perhaps «مُعْيِياً», exhausted]; and the vocative particle indicates that it is something inseparable, i.e. "O regret, this is your time"; this is the position of Sībawayh.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فِي جَنبِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ means in the matter of Allah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: in the side of Allah's command, by way of figurative representation (tamthīl).
That is: on the path that leads to the truth, which is faith.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلَىٰ قَدْ جَآءَتْكَ آيَاتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِهَا وَٱسْتَكْبَرْتَ وَكُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
﴿بَلَىٰ﴾ in the speech of the Arabs occurs only after a negation, and there is no negation in the speech, but its meaning is there, because the meaning of ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللهَ هَدَانِي﴾ is: Allah did not guide me.
And al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas narrated from Umm Salama that the Prophet ﷺ read: ﴿بَلَى قَدْ جَاءَتْكِ آياتِي، فَكَذَّبْتِ بِهَا وَاسْتَكْبَرْتِ، وَكُنْتِ مِنَ الكَافِرِينَ﴾ [i.e. with the feminine kasra on the tāʾ].
And the reading of al-Aʿmash is ﴿بَلَى قَدْ جَاءَتْهُ آيَاتِي﴾, and this indicates the masculine.
And al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas did not meet Umm Salama; nevertheless the reading is permissible, because "nafs" (soul) applies to the masculine and the feminine.
And some of them rejected this reading, saying: if he puts kasra on the tāʾ, he must say "wa-kunti min al-kawāfir" or "min al-kāfirāt".
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not binding; do you not see that before it is ﴿أَنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ﴾, then He said ﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُ لَمِنْ السَّاخِرِينَ﴾, and did not say "min al-sawākhir", nor "min al-sākhirāt"?
And the implied construction (taqdīr) in Arabic with kasra on the tāʾ is: "and you (f.) were arrogant, and were among the whole [company] of mockers", or "among the people who mock", or "among the folk (qawm) who mock"; and "qawm" applies to men and women when they are together, and to men alone, as [the poet] said:
وَمَا أَدْرِي وَسَوفَ إِخَالُ أَدْرِي * أَقَومٌ آلُ حِصْنٍ أَمْ نِسَاءُ
(I do not know — and I think I shall come to know — whether the family of Ḥiṣn are men or women.)

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيُنَجِّي ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْاْ بِمَفَازَتِهِمْ﴾.
That is: by their deliverance from the Fire.
And it is read ﴿بِمَفَازَاتِهِمْ﴾; and the singular is better, because mafāza is in the sense of fawz (success).

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّهُ مَقَالِيدُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْخَاسِرُونَ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿مَقَالِيدُ﴾ means keys.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and the meaning of "His are the keys of the heavens and the earth" is: He is the Creator of what is in them, and the key to its door is in His hand, Mighty and Majestic is He. Then He said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْخَاسِرُونَ﴾, i.e. whoever claims that another than He created anything of this has lost and disbelieved.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
Then He informed that He alone ought to be worshipped, and said after the proofs:
﴿قُلْ أَفَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ تَأْمُرُونِّيۤ أَعْبُدُ أَيُّهَا ٱلْجَاهِلُونَ﴾.
That is: Is it other than Allah that I should worship, at your command?
This is the view of Sībawayh.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿUbayda holds that the meaning is: they did not know Allah as He truly should be known.
And there is another view on its meaning, namely that the implied construction is: "they did not value the blessings of Allah", then [the muḍāf] was omitted, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلأَرْضُ جَمِيعـاً قَبْضَـتُهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ وَٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: all of this is in His right hand.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of ﴿وَٱلأَرْضُ جَمِيعـاً قَبْضَـتُهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾ is: He owns it, as you say: "this is in my grasp."
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: the meaning of ﴿بِيَمِينِهِ﴾ is: by His power, and he recited:
إِذَا مَا رَايَةٌ رُفِعَتْ لِمَجْدٍ * تَلَقَّاهَا عَرَابَةُ باليَمِينِ
(Whenever a banner is raised for glory, ʿArāba receives it with the right hand.)
That is, with strength.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: that it is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he was asked about al-ṣūr, and he said: it is a horn that is blown into.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda concerning His saying ﴿وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾: he said: into the forms (ṣuwar) of all people.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not well known; what is used as the plural of ṣūra is ṣuwar, and no one has read "wa-nufikha fī al-ṣuwar".
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda: ﴿فَصَعِقَ﴾: so he died.
And ʿĀṣim narrated from ʿĪsā al-Madanī, who said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn asking Kaʿb al-Aḥbār about His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾, and Kaʿb said: "Jibrāʾīl", "Mīkāʾīl" and "Isrāfīl", the angel of death, and the bearers of the Throne; then Allah causes them to die afterwards.
And Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated from Yazīd al-Raqāshī, from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾: he said: "Jibrāʾīl, Mīkāʾīl, the bearers of the Throne, the angel of death, and Isrāfīl."
And in this ḥadīth: the last of them to die is Jibrāʾīl ﷺ.
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾: they are the martyrs, girded with swords around the Throne.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this does not contradict the first.
And Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: (The trumpet will be blown, and I shall be the first to rise, and there will be Mūsā ﷺ; and I do not know whether he rose before me, or whether he is among those whom Allah excepted).
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخْرَىٰ فَإِذَا هُمْ قِيَامٌ يَنظُرُونَ﴾.
Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Between the two blasts there are forty."
Al-Ḥasan said: I do not know whether it is forty years, or forty months, or forty nights, or forty hours.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَشْرَقَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّهَا﴾.
This is made clear by the ḥadīth traced back (marfūʿ) to the Prophet ﷺ through many sound chains: (You will look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; you will not be wronged in seeing Him).
And it is narrated in four ways: "lā tuḍāmūna", "lā tuḍārūna", "lā tuḍārrūna" and "lā tuḍāmmūna".
So the meaning of (tuḍāmūna) is: no injustice (ḍaym) will befall you, as befalls [people] in this world in looking at kings.
And (lā tuḍārūna): no harm (ḍayr) will befall you.
And (lā tuḍāmmūna): you will not crowd up to one another so that one asks another to show him.
And (lā tuḍārrūna): you will not disagree with one another; one says ḍārartuhu muḍārratan wa-ḍirāran, i.e. I disagreed with him.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْاْ رَبَّهُمْ إِلَى ٱلّجَنَّةِ زُمَراً، حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا﴾.
The Kufans hold that the wāw is redundant (zāʾida).
And this is wrong according to the Basrans, because the wāw conveys the meaning of conjunction, and it is not permissible for it to be redundant.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: the meaning is: until, when they came to it and its gates were opened, they were happy [Translator's note: i.e. the apodosis is omitted].
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ لَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُـمْ طِبْتُمْ فَٱدْخُلُوهَا خَالِدِينَ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is: "you have been good, so enter it, abiding forever" — they entered; and this was omitted because the hearer knows it.
And it is said: the meaning of ﴿طِبْتُمْ﴾ is: you were good in the world.
And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, that he said: "They wash in a river in the Garden and drink from it, and no impurity or rancour remains in their insides but it comes out."

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَـالُواْ ٱلْحَـمْدُ للَّهِ ٱلَّذِي صَدَقَنَا وَعْدَهُ وَأَوْرَثَنَا ٱلأَرْضَ﴾.
Qatāda said: meaning the land of the Garden.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَقِيلَ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
So He concluded with praise, as He began with it.
